context.requirement_text:
Source: GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016): 'the process validator checks
that the referenced nodes exist and precede the node', AMENDED by BA
decision 2026-10-07: a named node may lie on a PARALLEL branch (no
path between the two nodes); strict precedence applies only when the
named node is on the same path as this node. Plus the
design-intent constraint that the REQ-455 validator WARNS (not a
violation) when distinct_from names a node that routes to the same
single-member role (the node could never complete). Adds checks
beside the existing node-attribute checks in
lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex and the install-time role warnings
added by REQ-455 (unbound task roles are reported as a warning list,
never an automatic binding).

BUILDS:
RESERVED CODES (copy exactly from REQ-459 design section 1.2; do
not invent others). Violations: `:invalid_distinct_from`,
`:distinct_from_on_non_human_task`, `:distinct_from_self_reference`,
`:distinct_from_unknown_node`, `:distinct_from_not_human_task`,
`:distinct_from_downstream_only`. Warning (string prefix, not an
atom): `distinct_from_single_member_role:`. They extend
Graph.Violation.code(); checks are CHK-26 (check_distinct_from/1,
checks 1 and 2) and CHK-27 (check_distinct_from_position/1, check 3),
appended after CHK-25 in Graph.validate_node_attributes/1.

1. Shape: `distinct_from` on a HUMAN_TASK is a list of non-empty node
   ids without duplicates and without the node's own id; on any other
   node type it is a violation. Codes: :invalid_distinct_from (not a
   list, non-string or empty entry, duplicate),
   :distinct_from_on_non_human_task, :distinct_from_self_reference.
2. Existence: every listed id is a node of the same definition and a
   HUMAN_TASK; a missing id is a violation naming node and id
   (:distinct_from_unknown_node); an existing node that is not a
   HUMAN_TASK is :distinct_from_not_human_task.
3. Path position: a listed node must not be reachable only AFTER this
   node (this node has a path to it and it has no path to this node):
   a node downstream-only is a violation naming both, since it can
   never have completed when this node is checked
   (:distinct_from_downstream_only). A listed node that precedes this
   node, is on a parallel or mutually exclusive branch (no path
   either way) or is on a rework loop (a path both ways) passes
   (design section 1.5 relation table). Consequence: three parallel
   nodes may each name the other two; a node and its own downstream
   successor may not name each other (l1-approval naming l2-approval
   fails). A node unreachable from START passes (CHK-22 reports it).
4. Same-role WARNING: when this node and a listed node route to the
   same role (attributes["role"] only, not escalation_role) and that
   role has exactly one member in the installing tenant, the
   validation result carries a WARNING (not a violation, prefix
   `distinct_from_single_member_role:`) naming both nodes and the
   role, because the single member could never complete the second
   node. One warning per unordered pair (ids sorted); it applies to
   preceding, parallel and loop pairs alike; zero members is the
   unbound_task_role: case, not this one. Evaluated where tenant role
   membership is known: pack install and
   Definitions.validate_definition_graph/2 (which already holds the
   tenant prefix), NOT in the activate response (record-shaped,
   carries no warnings) and not at pure Graph validation without a
   tenant. New RoleBinding functions single_member_pairs/1,
   member_counts/2 (one prefix-scoped query over group_members and
   tenant_role, returns counts only, run only when a definition has
   a candidate pair) and format_single_member_warning/2; the warning
   is the third source of ValidationWarnings.for_definitions/2
   (created by REQ-461). Members are counted as distinct
   group_members.user_id of the role's bound group regardless of
   users.status (design OQ-2).
requirement_acceptance_criteria: one test per check 1 to 3 with a minimal definition that violates only that check, asserting the code, the node id and the listed id; one passing neighbour per check

a distinct_from naming the node itself (:distinct_from_self_reference), a non-existent id (:distinct_from_unknown_node), a service-task id (:distinct_from_not_human_task), a duplicate (:invalid_distinct_from), and a node reachable only after this node (:distinct_from_downstream_only) are each reported (five negative tests); a non-list value is :invalid_distinct_from and the attribute on a non-HUMAN_TASK node is :distinct_from_on_non_human_task; each asserts the reserved code from the REQ-459 design section 1.2, no other code name

parallel branches: nodes P1, P2, P3 after a fork, each naming the other two, produce no violation; a listed node on the same path before this node passes; a listed node on a rework loop (path both ways) passes

check 4: a definition installed in a tenant where the shared role has one member returns a WARNING naming both nodes and the role, and the definition still installs (status unchanged); in a tenant where the role has two members no warning is returned

a distinct_from check never changes a definition (activation of a definition with only a warning succeeds, warnings never block); the distinct_from_single_member_role: warning appears in the pack-install `warnings` and the POST /definitions/:id/validate 200 body (not in the activate response)
every shipped definition is run through the validator in a test; for each, the count of new findings is quoted; shipped definitions without distinct_from report none
mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, scoped mix test over test/letflow/definitions, and mix letflow.check_boundaries pass, real output quoted

SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict recorded: check 4's member_counts/2 is a new query over group_members and tenant_role (the design confirms the condition is met); it is prefix-scoped (INV-1) and returns counts only, never user ids, names or emails (INV-2)

result.summary: PASS. Code in 7befe9f9 matches design 1.1/1.2/1.5 and the REQ-464 adjustments: six violation atoms exactly (graph.ex Violation.code() type), prefix distinct_from_single_member_role:, CHK-26 check_distinct_from/1 and CHK-27 check_distinct_from_position/1 appended after check_required_outputs (CHK-25) in validate_node_attributes/1, relation table implemented (violation only when MapSet.member?(reach[id], other) and not MapSet.member?(reach[other], id)), single_member_pairs/1, member_counts/2 (one query, [] -> no query, count(m.user_id, :distinct), no users join, Repo.all(prefix:), counts only), format_single_member_warning/2, third source in ValidationWarnings.for_definitions/2. Only call sites of ValidationWarnings are Definitions.validate_definition_graph/2 (definitions.ex:1287) and SolutionPack (solution_pack.ex:1410); activate does not use it. No mix run (read-only step).

issues.text: Reachability is pure node-to-node path existence over all resolved edges, not reachability from START. Design 1.5 table is path-based so this matches the table, but the design/requirement sentence 'a node unreachable from START passes' holds only for an isolated node: an orphan N with a path N->X (X reachable, no X->N) is flagged downstream_only. Recommend one test pinning the intended behaviour (isolated orphan passes); no code change needed under 'design wins'.

Fixtures that build distinct_from definitions (test/support/sod_support.ex chain_graph/loop/parallel, test/letflow/engine_distinct_from_test.exs esc_graph/timer_graph, routers/tasks_distinct_from_test.exs) were read: all name preceding, loop, parallel or escalation-predecessor nodes, so CHK-27 should accept them, but this was not run (read-only). The chain_graph(n3_names) callers pass arbitrary names: TEST step must run each of the four REQ-463 files separately to confirm.

design_vs_code_differences: CHK-27 uses flow_adjacency/3 + walk/2 (graph.ex:798,815) instead of build_adjacency/2 named in design 1.2. ACCEPTED: same resolved-edges-only forward closure (dangling edges dropped, as build_adjacency); walk includes the source node itself, harmless because other != id is filtered. Design cites build_adjacency only as the source of 'resolved edges'.

Extra public function RoleBinding.single_member_warnings_for_definitions/2 (not named in design). ACCEPTED: it is the implementation of the 'third source' glue, keeps the one-query-only-when-candidate rule across all definitions, returns [String.t()]; no type change.
single_member_pairs/1 spec returns [task_role()] (same map shape %{role_name, node_ids} as design).
Wire text identical to design: 'distinct_from_single_member_role: <role> (definition '<name>', nodes: <idA>, <idB>)', ids sorted.

CHK-26 emits one violation per defect and skips existence checks for malformed/self entries; null treated as absent; [] on HUMAN_TASK passes; distinct_from key on non-HUMAN_TASK (non-null, even []) violates. All consistent with design 1.1/1.2.
design_vs_requirement_differences: None found on detail: requirement text and design agree on codes, checks, warning placement and OQ-2 counting.
acceptance_criteria_walk: AC1 per-check tests: satisfiable; each check emits its own code naming node id and listed id in the message (self/unknown/not_human/downstream messages name both).
AC2 five negative tests + non-list (:invalid_distinct_from) + non-HUMAN_TASK (:distinct_from_on_non_human_task): satisfiable; duplicate yields :invalid_distinct_from.
AC3 parallel P1/P2/P3, preceding, loop: satisfiable by relation logic (neither/ reach(X,N) / both ways pass).

AC4 one-member warning vs two-member none: satisfiable (== 1 only; 0 members absent from counts map -> no warning, left to unbound_task_role:); definition install unaffected since warnings never block.
AC5 warning in pack install warnings and validate 200 body, not activate: satisfiable; only those two sites call ValidationWarnings.
AC6 shipped definitions: no shipped definition uses distinct_from (grep of priv/ found none), so new findings should be zero; test must quote count.

AC7 compile/format/test/check_boundaries: not run here (read-only); import Ecto.Query only: [from: 2] with count/2 inside from macro and 'for ... uniq: true do end |> Enum.sort_by' look valid but are unverified.

AC8 SECURITY-REVIEWER: member_counts/2 uses Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix) and Repo.all(prefix: prefix) (INV-1, applies to joined tables), select {t.name, count(distinct user_id)} only (INV-2). Condition is met; SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict still required from that agent.
